title: openai-compatible redundant `reasoningEffort` field in request body
body: ### Description When using openai-compatible provider and specifying the `reasoningEffort` option, both `reasoning_effort` and `reasoningEffort` fields appear in the request body, with the latter being redundant. Some providers will raise an error due to this. ``` providerOptions: { 'provider-name': { reasoningEffort: 'low' } } ``` When specifying `reasoning_effort` directly instead of `reasoningEffort`, both fields in the request body disappear: ``` providerOptions: { 'provider-name': { reasoning_effort: 'low' } } ``` The key of the problem should be here: https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/8d6d8d70a19d8bb93363bcd26063518449b5223f/packages/openai-compatible/src/chat/openai-compatible-chat-language-model.ts#L186-L192 There should be a way to add only the `reasoning_effort` field to the request body ### AI SDK Version - ai: 5.0.22 - @ai-sdk/openai-compatible: 1.0.11 ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

linked_prs.title: fix(openai-compatible): prevent redundant reasoningEffort field
linked_prs.body:
Prevent redundant `reasoningEffort` field alongside `reasoning_effort` in request body.

Fixes #8372

## Background

See #8372. Some OpenAI compatible backends (like LiteLLM proxying to Azure, which is what I can personally test) are tripping over the `reasoningEffort` field with errors like:

```
AzureException BadRequestError - Unknown parameter: 'reasoningEffort'
```

## Summary

I decided to NOT forward (spread) any of the "known" `openaiCompatibleProviderOptions` to avoid duplication. The idea is that these are already added to the correct part of the request body anyway. Why else would they be parsed out?
